verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a crewed mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "NASA's Artemis II astronauts" (R1); "four astronauts" (R2); "carrying NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly describe Artemis II as carrying a crew of astronauts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 1, 2026" launch timestamps (R1); "set to launch on April 1, 2026" (R4); "targeted launch time of 6:24 p.m. on Wednesday, April 1" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm the scheduled and actual launch date as April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R1); "Kennedy Space Center in Florida" (R2); "Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B" (R3)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch window opens at 6:24 p.m. EDT" (R1); "at 6:24 p.m. EDT" (R3); "6:24 p.m. ET" (R7)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify the launch window opening at exactly 6:24 p.m. EDT/ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission aims for a ~10-day trip around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "about nine and a half days" (R1); "10-day mission" (R2); "approximately 10-day Artemis II mission" (R3); "10-day mission" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe the mission duration as approximately 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission will travel roughly 252,799 miles from Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "252,000 miles" approx. (R1); "252,799 miles" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: R2 matches the exact distance; R1 rounds it closely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashdown is planned in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R1); "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R2); "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean" (R5)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission splashdown is planned for April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown on April 10" (R1); "splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10" (R2); "splashed down... on 10 April" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm splashdown date as April 10.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch site is Kennedy Space Center, Launch Complex 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch Complex 39B" (R1); "Launch Complex 39B" (R2); "Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B" (R3)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration is ~10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "nine and a half days" (R1); "10-day mission" (R5)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes an initial orbit of ~24 hours checking systems in Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "spending about 24 hours orbiting the Earth while they put their Orion capsule through its paces" (R1); "orbit around the Earth for about 24 hours" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on ~24-hour initial Earth orbit for system checks.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II trans-lunar injection is scheduled to send the crew towards the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "trans-lunar injection," or TLI, will boost them on a path to the moon" (R1); "translunar injection (TLI) burn" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm TLI sends crew to Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II lunar flyby follows an approx. four-day journey to the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "roughly a four-day journey to the far side of the moon" (R1); "four days" outbound (R5)

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch window is 5:24–7:24 pm CT (6:24–8:24 pm ET).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "5:24 pm CT, and the window is 5:24–7:24 pm CT" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Exact match, with time zone conversion accurate.

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 2 at 6:22 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 2: 6:22 pm CDT" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Precise match for backup date and time.

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 3 at 7:00 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 3: 7:00 pm CDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 4 at 7:53 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 4: 7:53 pm CDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 5 at 8:40 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 5: 8:40 pm CDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 6 at 9:36 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 6: 9:36 pm CDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 30 at 5:06 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "April 30: 5:06 pm CDT" (R4)

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Day 1 includes launch to Earth orbit and initial checkouts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Launch day... first eight minutes... into space... systems checks" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: R5 describes Day 1 as launch, orbit, prox ops, and initial checks.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Days 2-3 include trans-lunar injection, safety checks, and system tests.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: Flight day 2: TLI; Flight day 3: safety demonstrations (R5)
verifications.reasoning: TLI on day 2, safety checks on day 3, but not all explicitly grouped as claimed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Day 4 includes lunar flyby, lunar imaging, and trajectory adjustments.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: Flight day 4: outbound, correction burn, imaging practice (R5); Day four: photo Earth moon (R6); lunar flyby Day 6 (R5, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Flyby is on Day 6, not Day 4; Day 4 is still outbound.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Day 7 includes journey back to Earth, leaving the lunar sphere of influence.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Flight day 7: Orion will exit lunar space... journey back" (R5)

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Days 8-9 include radiation protection tests and manual steering tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Flight day 8: radiation shielding, attitude control (steering); Flight day 9: preparations (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Day 8 matches exactly; Day 9 more prep but fits broadly.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission Day 10 includes re-entry, parachute deployment, and splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Flight day 10: Atmospheric reentry and splashdown... parachute" (R5)
